the_latest_census: The 2006 census is Nigeria's latest. The volume's preface (printed page 3) records the provisional result in Official Gazette No. 4, Vol. 94 of 19 January 2007 and the final result in Gazette No. 2, Vol. 96 of 2 February 2009, and says "the questions on how many we are in Nigeria should now be satisfactorily put to rest". That the results were disputed is not cited here: no open page saying so was read for this transcription.

transcription.by: read from the PDF's text layer (pdftotext -layout), every number taken from it, not typed; pages 20, 32, 48, 56 and 58 also checked against the rendered page image
transcription.as_published: names, spellings and serial numbers as printed, upper case as printed. Joined where the print wraps a name over two lines: Oyo S/No. 6 IBADAN CENTRAL [IBADAN NORTH EAST], and the Adamawa total row ADAMAWA STATE. The FCT's total row prints ABUJA FCT (heading ABUJA – FCT).
transcription.corrections: none: no number in the text layer was garbled, and every row passed the checks as read
as_printed_and_kept: Serial numbers: Taraba runs 1 to 15 then 17 (16 LGAs, as the volume's list of states gives); Benue runs 1 to 19 then 21 to 24 (23 LGAs); Akwa Ibom prints 234 for 23 (OKOBO) and 256 for 25 (ORON), and has no 26 (31 LGAs, the last numbered 32). Checked on the page image for Taraba and Akwa Ibom: the misprints are in the print, not the text layer.

Taraba State prints a row "* DISPUTED AREAS" with senatorial district 0, no land size and no footnote for the asterisk: 10106 men, 9858 women, 19964 total. It is counted in the state total; it is kept as its own row (level: disputed areas), not as an LGA.

Legends cut short in print (checked on the page image): Jigawa "C = Jigawa Noth We", Cross River "C = Cross River", Akwa Ibom "C =" with no name. The letter is kept; the name as printed, empty for Akwa Ibom C.
Lagos legend prints "C = Lagos Weast"; kept as printed.
Oyo's page heads its last column Persons, the others Both Sexes.

units: counts.csv: the country (printed page 9), 36 states and the FCT (each state page's total row), and 774 LGAs with their state and senatorial district, plus one row of disputed areas in Taraba State. The six zones on page 9 are not transcribed.

reviewed.found: First transcription. The 2006 census is the latest.

offered.why: Fieldwork offers each level as its own table, with geoBoundaries' name for each unit, so the census relates to a map of the states or of the LGAs without anyone retyping a name. The printed counts (counts.csv) stay here as the source, and every check runs on them.

states.label: Its 37 states, with geoBoundaries' names
states.what: The 36 states and the FCT with the name geoBoundaries gives each, written by scripts/nigeria_today.py. Counts as printed.
states.how: The volume prints "JIGAWA STATE"; geoBoundaries writes "Jigawa". Each printed name, without " STATE" and in title case, is geoBoundaries' NGA ADM1 name; ABUJA FCT is "Abuja Federal Capital Territory".

boundaries.what: geoBoundaries gbOpen NGA ADM1 and ADM2 at commit 9469f09 (GRID3, 2022, CC BY 4.0), the simplified files, read and not kept here

does_not_establish: That geoBoundaries' state lines are the census's: they are GRID3's, 2022.

lgas.label: Its 774 LGAs, with geoBoundaries' names
lgas.what: The 774 Local Government Areas with the name geoBoundaries gives each, and their state, written by scripts/nigeria_today.py. Counts as printed. Taraba's disputed-areas row (19,964 persons) is not an LGA and is left out; it stays in counts.csv.
lgas.how: geoBoundaries' ADM2 file does not say which state an LGA lies in, and some LGA names occur in two states. Each ADM2 unit is placed in the ADM1 state its polygon lies in, and each printed LGA matched by name within its state, ignoring case, spaces and punctuation. 31 are spelled differently in the two sources and are paired by a list in the script (Egbado North and South are geoBoundaries' Yewa North and South). Two, Tsafe (Zamfara) and Akoko South East (Ondo), have polygons that fall over a state line in the simplified files and are matched by their unique name.
